claim: BPS (Indonesia's official statistics agency) reports the CREATIVE ECONOMY workforce broadly -- not 'content creators' as a discrete category -- was 27.40 million people in 2025 (18.70% of national workforce), up from 26.48 million (18.30%) in 2024. This is a fundamentally different, much broader occupational category than the 'content creator' figures used elsewhere in this batch.
stance_target: the notion that any government 'content creator' figure (8 juta, 17 juta) traces to an official BPS census or survey
scope_conditions: Indonesia, national creative-economy workforce (culinary, fashion, gaming, music, film, design, digital content, etc. combined), 2024-2025
quoted_support: "Tahun 2025, tenaga kerja ekonomi kreatif mencakup sekitar 18,70 persen dari total tenaga kerja nasional atau mencapai sekitar 27,40 juta jiwa. Angka ini naik dari tahun sebelumnya, di mana tahun 2024 jumlah tenaga kerja ekonomi kreatif capai 26,48 juta jiwa (18,30 persen)."

claim: As of November 2025, BPS's chief statistician stated that the 2026 Economic Census (SE2026) would be the FIRST census to give a complete picture of creative-economy business actors including digital content creators -- confirming that no prior dedicated census-based count of Indonesian content creators exists.
stance_target: absence of an official, methodologically disclosed BPS count of content creators specifically
scope_conditions: Indonesia, national statistical infrastructure, as of Nov 2025 with SE2026 still pending
quoted_support: "SE2026 nantinya akan memberikan gambaran lengkap pelaku usaha kreatif di berbagai subsektor, seperti kuliner, fesyen, gim, musik, film, desain, hingga konten digital, termasuk lokasi dan skala usaha."
time_period: as of November 2025, SE2026 conducted in 2026

claim: West Java alone accounts for 6.24 million creative-economy workers, and West Java, Central Java, and East Java combined account for 57.81% of Indonesia's total creative-economy workforce -- indicating strong geographic concentration in Java.
stance_target: geographic distribution of Indonesia's creative-economy workforce
quoted_support: "Provinsi Jawa Barat (Jabar) tercatat sebagai wilayah dengan tenaga kerja ekonomi kreatif terbesar, yaitu 6,24 juta jiwa. Jika digabungkan, Jabar, Jawa Tengah (Jateng), dan Jawa Timur (Jateng) menyumbang 57,81 persen dari total tenaga kerja ekonomi kreatif nasional."
numbers: 57.81% combined share for West Java, Central Java, East Java
